content: Religious fasting practices, such as those observed during Ramadan and Yom Kippur, require individuals to abstain from food and drink for defined periods of time. For individuals with diabetes who choose to participate in these fasting practices, it is essential to provide education on how to effectively manage blood glucose levels during the fasting period. Adjustments to diabetes medications, including insulin or oral hypoglycemic agents, may be necessary to prevent hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia during fasting hours. Patients should also be counseled on maintaining safe levels of physical activity while fasting, as excessive exertion may increase the risk of glucose imbalances.
